issue.title: feat(jira): Add a read-only cloudId audit for Jira integrations

labels.name: repo-f814c484
labels.description: Automatically applied to PRs that change backend components

issue.body:
Adds `sentry.integrations.jira.cloud_id.audit_cloud_ids()`, a read-only check to run from a control silo shell before Jira integrations are rekeyed from the Connect clientKey to the site's cloudId (which Forge uses to identify a site). Nothing calls it automatically and it writes nothing.

For every Jira integration, including disabled ones since they still hold their `external_id`, it fetches the cloudId from the site's unauthenticated `/_edge/tenant_info` endpoint and reports:

- cloudIds shared by more than one integration, which would collide on `(provider, external_id)` after rekeying
- sites that no longer resolve (404 or no cloudId)
- renamed sites, where the stored base URL redirects to a new hostname
- base URLs that aren't Atlassian Cloud hosts, which are never requested

Requests go through `safe_urlopen`, only to `https` `*.atlassian.net` / `*.jira.com` hosts. `summary()` prints counts and `write_csv()` dumps per-integration results.

comment.body: Moving this to a getsentry job (getsentry/getsentry#23064), which is how one-off production audits run, instead of a module to call from a shell.

issue.title: feat(jira): Record Forge installations and use their system tokens

labels.name: repo-f814c484
labels.description: Automatically applied to PRs that change frontend components

labels.name: repo-f814c484
labels.description: Automatically applied to PRs that change backend components

issue.body:
Adds the endpoint Forge calls with a site's system token, and lets `JiraCloudClient` make API calls with that token instead of the Connect JWT.

Forge only hands a remote a system token when it calls it, so the app's `avi:forge:installed:app` / `avi:forge:upgraded:app` triggers and an hourly scheduled trigger all hit `/extensions/jira/forge/installation/` (control silo). The endpoint verifies the Forge invocation token, takes the site's cloud ID from the signed `apiBaseUrl` (backend invocations can have an empty `context`), and queues `sync_forge_installation` with the system token Fernet-encrypted so it stays out of task args and error reports. The system token is opaque, so its expiry is recorded as receipt time plus Atlassian's guaranteed two-hour minimum.

The task links the installation to the site's Jira integration and stores `metadata["forge"]` (installation, API base URL, token, expiry) under a row lock, ignoring a token older than the stored one:
- Forge apps listed in the new `jira.forge.native-app-ids` option have no Connect predecessor (e.g. the staging app), so their installs get a Forge-only integration keyed by cloud ID.
- Any other trusted Forge app is the Connect app's successor, so every site installing it also has a Connect integration. The task finds it by the Connect clientKey Atlassian exposes as a reserved app property, and retries if that lookup fails. A missing option entry therefore can't create a duplicate integration.

`JiraCloudClient` sends requests to `api.atlassian.com/ex/jira/<cloudId>` with the system token when:
- the integration is Forge-only (no Connect secret), or
- it's a Connect integration listed in the new `jira.forge.integration-ids` option (empty by default, so existing integrations are unchanged).

With less than 5 minutes left on the token, Connect integrations fall back to the Connect JWT; Forge-only ones raise `JiraForgeTokenUnavailable` (an `ApiUnauthorized`, so syncs halt) and emit `jira.forge.token_expired`.

Merge #129737 first: it makes Connect reinstalls merge metadata under a lock, which is what keeps `forge` from being wiped by a reinstall.

Also adds the staging Forge app manifest used to exercise this against sentry.io; its app ID is a placeholder. The `controlsiloUrlPatterns.ts` line is the generated pattern for the new control endpoint, required by `test_no_missing_urls`; the frontend never calls it, so deploy order doesn't matter.

comment.body: Both fixed in the latest commit: a Connect JWT naming a Forge-only integration is now rejected as an invalid token (with a test), and the staging manifest mentions `jira.forge.native-app-ids` too.

comment.body: Ha, yeah. It might have one inside, but Atlassian says the OAuth tokens (and any JWT claims in them) "need to be treated as Opaque" and aren't part of any published API, so we shouldn't decode them. What they do guarantee is that the system token "is valid for a min TTL of 2 hours", so we record receipt time + 2h. The hourly trigger keeps that well ahead of the 5-minute cutoff the client uses. https://developer.atlassian.com/platform/forge/remote/essentials/

+"""Verification of Forge Invocation Tokens (FITs).
+
+Every request a Forge app sends to a remote backend carries a FIT in its
+`Authorization: Bearer` header: an RS256 JWT signed by Atlassian that names the
+app, the installation and the site it was sent for.
+
+https://developer.atlassian.com/platform/forge/remote/essentials/
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import logging
+from collections.abc import Mapping
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from typing import Any
+
+import orjson
+from django.core.cache import cache
+from jwt import ExpiredSignatureError, PyJWTError
+
+from sentry import options
+from sentry.http import safe_urlopen
+from sentry.utils import jwt
+
+logger = logging.getLogger("sentry.integrations.jira.forge")
+
+FORGE_JWKS_URL = "https://forge.cdn.prod.atlassian-dev.net/.well-known/jwks.json"
+FORGE_INVOCATION_TOKEN_ISSUER = "forge/invocation-token"
+
+_JWKS_CACHE_KEY = "jira-forge:jwks"
+_JWKS_CACHE_SECONDS = 60 * 60
+_JWKS_REFRESH_LOCK_KEY = "jira-forge:jwks:refreshed"
+# Tokens name their key, so this stops tokens with made-up key ids from forcing a
+# fetch on every request.
+_JWKS_MIN_REFRESH_SECONDS = 60
+_JWKS_FETCH_TIMEOUT = 5
+
+
+class ForgeInvocationTokenError(Exception):
+    pass
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class ForgeInvocation:
+    """The verified claims of a FIT that we act on."""
+
+    app_id: str
+    # Stable across app upgrades, but changes if the app is uninstalled and reinstalled.
+    installation_id: str
+    # Where Atlassian API calls for this installation go, e.g.
+    # `https://api.atlassian.com/ex/jira/<cloudId>`. Not the site URL.
+    api_base_url: str
+    cloud_id: str | None
+    environment_type: str | None
+    module_key: str | None
+    # The invoking user's account ID. Only present for calls from UI modules.
+    principal: str | None
+
+
+def _fetch_public_keys() -> dict[str, str]:
+    response = safe_urlopen(FORGE_JWKS_URL, method="GET", timeout=_JWKS_FETCH_TIMEOUT)
+    response.raise_for_status()
+    keys: dict[str, str] = {}
+    for jwk in response.json().get("keys", []):
+        if jwk.get("kty") == "RSA" and isinstance(jwk.get("kid"), str):
+            keys[jwk["kid"]] = jwt.rsa_key_from_jwk(orjson.dumps(jwk).decode())
+    return keys
+
+
+def _public_key_for(kid: str) -> str:
+    keys: dict[str, str] | None = cache.get(_JWKS_CACHE_KEY)
+    # Atlassian rotates keys, so an unknown kid triggers a refresh, at most once a minute.
+    if keys is None or (
+        kid not in keys and cache.add(_JWKS_REFRESH_LOCK_KEY, True, _JWKS_MIN_REFRESH_SECONDS)
+    ):
+        try:
+            keys = _fetch_public_keys()
+        except Exception as e:
+            logger.warning("jira.forge.jwks_fetch_failed", exc_info=True)
+            raise ForgeInvocationTokenError("Unable to fetch Forge signing keys") from e
+        cache.set(_JWKS_CACHE_KEY, keys, _JWKS_CACHE_SECONDS)
+
+    key = keys.get(kid)
+    if key is None:
+        raise ForgeInvocationTokenError("Unknown signing key")
+    return key
+
+
+def _cloud_id(claims: Mapping[str, Any]) -> str | None:
comment.body: Atlassian documents the payload, but which fields show up depends on how the app was invoked, and the claims come off the wire untyped, so the `.get()` chains are deliberate. `ForgeInvocation` is the typed result we hand to callers. Dropped the `_cloud_id` helper too, so the remaining parsing is just the few `.get()`s in the return.

issue.title: fix(jira): Accept expired webhook tokens only from control-signed deliveries

labels.name: repo-f814c484
labels.description: Automatically applied to PRs that change backend components

issue.body:
Jira `issue_updated` webhooks are verified in control on arrival, then replayed to the cell through the webhook mailbox, where `JiraIssueUpdatedWebhook` verifies the Connect JWT again. Atlassian's tokens expire within minutes, so a webhook that waits in the mailbox past that is rejected with a 409, and the outbox drops 409s without retrying. Each drop is a Jira → Sentry status, assignee or issue-move sync that never happens.

This PR had control sign each replayed delivery so the cell could accept an expired Connect token only when that signature verified.

comment.body: Closing: adding a new control-signed delivery path is more than this fix should take on right now. The expired-token drop is still a real problem and needs a smaller approach.

issue.title: feat(jira): Add JiraForgeInstallation model

labels.name: repo-f814c484
labels.description: Automatically applied to PRs that change backend components

issue.body:
Adds `JiraForgeInstallation`, a control-silo table linking each Jira Cloud integration to its site's Forge identity: a unique `cloud_id`, plus the Forge `installation_id` once the site has sent a Forge request. Nothing reads or writes it yet.

Forge requests identify a site by cloud ID instead of the Connect `clientKey` stored in `Integration.external_id`, and `Integration.metadata` is encrypted, so it can't be queried. This table is how Forge requests will find their integration during the Connect → Forge migration. The cloud ID can be backfilled for existing integrations from the site URL, which is why `installation_id` is nullable.

This implements a proposal that's still in design review, so it shouldn't merge until that's settled.

comment.body: Closing. Review of the Forge migration doc moved identity to rekeying Jira integrations onto `cloudId` (`external_id = cloudId`), with Forge installation state in `Integration.metadata`, so this permanent mapping table isn't needed. A temporary `clientKey` → integration lookup for Connect requests will come later, at the rekey step.
